svg.title: Memento
svg.desc: Memento. Capture an object's state in a snapshot only it can read, so it can be restored later without breaking encapsulation. Step 1, Undo needs private state: History must remember the editor's state, but its fields are private, and a blur has no inverse. Step 2, A sealed snapshot: save() seals the editor's state in an EditorSnapshot; History keeps it unread; restore() unseals it. Step 3, Edit, snapshot, restore: Save, Brightness +20; save, Blur 3. Undo restores blur 0, then brightness 0: the exact pixels. Step 4, The cost, and the cousins: A 12 MP snapshot is 48 MB, ten are 480 MB: limit the history, save what changed, share the rest.

g.text: History must remember the editor's state, but its fields are private, and a blur has no inverse.
save() seals the editor's state in an EditorSnapshot; History keeps it unread; restore() unseals it.
Save, Brightness +20; save, Blur 3. Undo restores blur 0, then brightness 0: the exact pixels.
A 12 MP snapshot is 48 MB, ten are 480 MB: limit the history, save what changed, share the rest.

g.text: needs a copy of brightness, blur, pixels
10 undo steps of a 12 MP photo
History could copy them, but so could any other code:
and every caller now depends on how the editor stores its state
A blur replaces each pixel with the average of its neighbours:
many photos blur to the same pixels, so no inverse can undo it
Undo needs a copy of private state, and no inverse can undo a blur
ImageEditor (wide interface): brightness, blur and a copy of the pixels
History (narrow interface): only the label, such as “before Blur 3”
A snapshot is a sealed copy: History stores it, and only ImageEditor can open it
Each undo restores the exact saved pixels, blur and all: no inverse operation needed
keep the last N, drop the oldest
vs Command: undo by running an inverse operation, no snapshot. A command can keep a memento to undo itself.
Browsers: a state object per history.pushState() entry
Redux DevTools: time-travel debugging jumps to a stored state
Databases and VMs: snapshots to revert to after a bad change
Event sourcing: load a snapshot, replay only the newer events
